name: Rotating copper-disc generator
summary: Faraday spun a copper disc between magnet poles and drew a steady electric current from it, an early demonstration that motion and magnetism can generate electricity continuously.
description: A rotating copper disc passes between concentrated magnetic poles; sliding collectors at rim and axle feed a galvanometer, sustaining a deflection while rotation continues.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: One apparatus first drew steady current from motion for experimenters, and the line of electrical generators followed from that demonstration.

links.statement: Obtaining currents from magnets prompted Faraday to adapt Arago’s rotating-metal experiment into an electrical source, culminating in the disc and collectors.
links.alternatives: The earlier coil/magnet arrangement yields impulses; the rotating disc provides a sustained output. Arago’s rotating-metal experiment is an additional input awaiting its own dated node.
links.caveats: The edge is from the documented group of magnet-induced-current tests represented here by §39; it does not credit that single test as the sole cause.
links.timing: The same-year report explicitly places success in magnet-current tests before the stated generator objective, while rearranging detailed trials.

evidence.supports: States the motivation from the earlier magnet tests and describes sustained generation.
